key_insight: Symmetry-preserving variational circuits improve lattice Gross–Neveu energy estimates, while adaptive circuits enable parameter transfer to larger systems.
engineering_relevance: The adaptive construction offers linear precompilation local-factor growth with volume and a volume-independent shared-parameter count when flavor number, range caps, and append count are fixed.
method: Build fixed ansätze preserving total fermion number or each flavor number.
Use SC-ADAPT-VQE with bulk, boundary-sensitive, and cross-flavor generators.
Prepare sector-resolved excited states by sequential deflation and assess degenerate eigenspaces using projector fidelities.
evidence_signal: Classical benchmarks reach 30 qubits; selected massive fixed ansätze achieve relative energy errors of about 10⁻⁵–2×10⁻⁴, while one-flavor circuits transferred to 60–400 qubits show 0.35%–1.76% deviations from DMRG references without target-side optimization.
watch_item: Fixed-accuracy scaling to arbitrary volumes remains unestablished, and the reported evaluations are classical circuit and tensor-network benchmarks rather than quantum-hardware demonstrations.
paper_title: Symmetry-Preserving and Scalable Variational Circuits for the Lattice Gross-Neveu Model
